literal: Yali begot Bidie.
idiomatic: Yali had a son Bidie.

literal: Bidie begot Ling.
idiomatic: Bidie was the father of Ling.

literal: Ling begot Noulisi, who was magnanimous and few in desires; his orders were not strict yet the people were transformed—he is known as Emperor Suzu.
idiomatic: Ling's son Noulisi was broad-minded and sparing in wants; though his rule was mild, the people were naturally swayed—this was Emperor Suzu.

literal: Suzu begot Salade, who once fought the Yellow Shiwei in battle; arrows pierced through several quivers—he is known as Emperor Yizu.
idiomatic: Suzu had Salade, who once duelled the Yellow Shiwei; arrows ran through stack upon stack of quivers—this was Emperor Yizu.

literal: Yizu begot Jundeshi, who first taught the people agriculture, excelled at animal husbandry, and the state grew rich—he is known as Emperor Xuanzu.
idiomatic: Yizu begot Jundeshi, who first taught grain-growing, kept fine herds, and made the country wealthy—this was Emperor Xuanzu.

literal: Xuanzu begot Saladi, who loved the people and cherished things, first established ironworks, and taught people smelting and casting—he is known as Emperor Dezu, Taizu's father.
idiomatic: Xuanzu had Saladi, humane toward the people and tender toward things; he founded ironworks and taught folk to smelt and cast—this was Emperor Dezu, father of Taizu.

literal: For generations they served as yilijin of the Khitan Yaolian clan, holding governmental power.
idiomatic: For generations they held the yilijinship of the Khitan Yaolian line and wielded the reins of power.

literal: Dezu's younger brother Shuluo campaigned north against the Jue and Shiwei, raided south into Yi, Ding, and Xi; he first promoted rammed-earth construction, established towns, taught people to plant mulberry and hemp and practice weaving—already harboring ambitions for broad territory and a large population.
idiomatic: Dezu's brother Shuluo marched north against the Jue and Shiwei and south against Yi, Ding, and Xi; he introduced rammed-earth building, founded towns, taught mulberry and hemp planting and weaving—the ambition for broad lands and a populous realm was already plain.

literal: Then Taizu received the khan's abdication in his favor and thereupon founded the state.
idiomatic: Then Taizu received the khan's surrender of the throne and founded the kingdom.

literal: Campaigning east and west, like snapping withered stalks and pulling rotten wood.
idiomatic: East and west his campaigns went, snapping dry wood and pulling rotten timber.

literal: East from the sea, west to the drifting sands, north cutting across the great desert—trust and majesty for ten thousand li, two hundred years in duration—could this be the work of a single day!
idiomatic: From the eastern sea to the western wastes, from the northern desert to ten thousand li of sway—a realm two centuries in the making: was that the work of a single day?

literal: When the Duke of Zhou executed Guan and Cai, none could find fault with him.
idiomatic: When the Duke of Zhou put Guan and Cai to death, no one faulted him for it.

literal: In the rebellion of Gege and Anduan, Taizu spared their lives and then employed them again—is this not beyond the measure of a ruler?
idiomatic: In the rebellions of Gege and Anduan, Taizu spared them and then put them back in office—was that truly the measure of a prince?

literal: The old histories' account of the Fuyu affair is also strange indeed!
idiomatic: How strange too is the old histories' tale of the Fuyu crisis!

literal: Collation Notes
idiomatic: Collation Notes

literal: 1: "Tang military governor of the Yiwu Army Wang Chuzhi Tang" — the original erroneously read "Jin."
idiomatic: 1: Tang's military governor of the Yiwu Army, Wang Chuzhi — for Tang, the original text wrongly read Jin.

literal: According to juan 75 Biography of Wang Yu, Old History of the Five Dynasties juan 54, and Sima Guang's Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government
idiomatic: According to juan 75, Biography of Wang Yu; Old History of the Five Dynasties, juan 54; and Sima Guang's Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government

literal: (hereinafter abbreviated as Comprehensive Mirror)]〉
idiomatic: (hereinafter abbreviated as Comprehensive Mirror)]〉

literal: Corrected accordingly.
idiomatic: Corrected accordingly.

literal: 2: "Adjutant general Zhang Chong Zhang Chong" — New History of the Five Dynasties juan 47 and Old History juan 88 biographies both read Zhang Xichong.
idiomatic: 2: "Adjutant general Zhang Chong Zhang Chong" — New History of the Five Dynasties, juan 47, and Old History, juan 88, biographies both read Zhang Xichong.

literal: This avoids the taboo name of Tianzuo's son Yenxi; the character xi was removed.
idiomatic: This avoids the taboo name of Tianzuo's son Yenxi; the character xi was dropped.

literal: 3: "Dug the Jin River and took Wushan stone" — the characters for "dug" and "took" are transposed.
idiomatic: 3: "Dug the Jin River and took Wushan stone" — the words dug and took are transposed.

literal: 4: "Guo Cunqian killed his lord Cun Cunqian" — New History juan 73 reads Congqian.
idiomatic: 4: "Guo Cunqian killed his lord Cun Cunqian" — New History of the Five Dynasties, juan 73, reads Congqian.

literal: 5: "Lulong acting military governor Zhang Chong rebelled and fled to Tang" — regarding Zhang's flight to Tang, Old History juan 39 and Comprehensive Mirror both place it in the third year of Tiancheng
idiomatic: 5: "Lulong field marshal Zhang Chong rebelled and fled to Tang" — regarding Zhang's flight to Tang, Old History of the Five Dynasties, juan 39, and Comprehensive Mirror both place the event in the third year of Tiancheng

literal: (Liao Tianxian year 3)]〉
idiomatic: (Liao Tianxian year 3)]〉

literal: Intercalary eighth month.
idiomatic: intercalary eighth month.
